# mapserver / mapfuzzer

mapserver's own fuzz target `mapfuzzer` ([source](source/mapfuzzer.c), modified; see below), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over MapServer (MapServer/MapServer at fbcb5754).

Writes the input (Size from 10 to 10240 bytes) to a new file named by CPLGenerateTempFilename(NULL) with .map (a suffix msLoadMap's default mapfile name pattern accepts) appended, loads it as a mapfile with msLoadMap(filename, NULL, NULL) and frees what that returns with msFreeMap, then deletes the file with VSIUnlink, frees the name and clears MapServer's error list with msResetErrorList. It returns -1 for an input with Size below 10 or above 10240, returns 0 without loading anything when fopen cannot open the file for writing, and drops the results of fwrite, fclose and VSIUnlink.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against MapServer at commit fbcb5754.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source is modified: source/mapfuzzer.c is MapServer fbcb5754's fuzzers/mapfuzzer.c with two Theorem Labs changes: its length check returns -1, not 1, for an input outside its limits (libFuzzer rejects the input; the driver exits 0, not 78), and it returns 0, not 1, when fopen cannot open the temporary file, so the driver does not exit with status 78 for that call.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing. Its halts statements say only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer. Its agreement statements say only that the code never crashes or trips a sanitizer, and allow a run that never ends.

## Statements ([Statements.v](Statements.v))

**Blocked by the model.** On ordinary inputs each of these binaries removes files or directories, opens files other than its input and asks for its working directory, which this release's model treats as an error, so every statement here is false in this model for that reason alone. The program is not at fault; the statements become meaningful when the model covers it.
